Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second essay. The umpires are back in the middle and the Indian players can be seen in a huddle as well before taking their places on the field. It will be the duo of Henry Nicholls and Devon Conway to open the innings for New Zealand. Mohammed Siraj will get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

As seen so far, timing the ball hasn’t been straightforward on this slowish surface, and it could slow down further as the day wears on. A couple of dismissals have already underlined the point that anything not struck cleanly off the middle can quickly turn into trouble. Add to that the fact that no total has ever been successfully chased in the four ODIs played at Rajkot, and the task ahead becomes even more challenging for New Zealand. All in all, it sets up for a delicious second half ahead. Stick around as the chase is on the other side.

A 57-run partnership between Rahul and Nitish then kept the innings afloat for India, with the former scoring a fluent and valiant century as well. And when India needed that final act of acceleration, KL Rahul switched the gears in the final few overs and propelled India to a rather respectable total of 284. Honestly, at one stage, it didn't look achievable at all. Bowling-wise, New Zealand were not at all poor given how inexperienced this bowling lineup may look on paper. If we look at the distribution, interestingly, all the pacers conceded more than run-a-ball, but accounted for the most wickets. Whereas spinners, in their combined effort of 23 overs, were miserly, giving away only 89 runs, sharing just two scalps.

Rohit once again failed to convert his start, but the groundwork had been laid. Gill brought up a classy half-century before Jamieson struck to remove him, forcing India into another rebuilding phase. A prolonged boundary drought followed, almost for ten overs, and Kristian Clarke was rewarded for his discipline. The loss of Iyer and a well-set Kohli saw India slip from 99/1 to 118/4. With the seamers getting the ball to nip around and Bracewell exploiting the turn on offer, and choking the scoring effectively. India were in desperate need of momentum and, more importantly, a way to halt the slide. That stability came through a calm, measured stand between the experienced duo of KL Rahul and Ravindra Jadeja. The scoring rate never quite took off, hovering under 5s, but the pair did what the situation demanded, stitching together a 73-run partnership to steady the innings before Jadeja departed against the run of play.

It was a watchful start from the Indian openers as they took time to assess conditions. The ball moved around early, with Jamieson bowling two probing maidens and Zakary Foulkes getting the swing to talk. India crawled to just 10 in the first five overs, but anything loose was still put away. Once settled, Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill shifted gears smoothly, reeling off a flurry of boundaries. The next five overs yielded 47 runs, and India closed the Powerplay on a healthy 57 without loss.

A fantastic finish with a touch of KLass to this Indian innings. The hosts were pushed under pressure, getting reduced to 118/4, and needed someone to step up. KL Rahul was that man, who averted the crisis once again for his team. New Zealand bowled really well for almost 90 percent of the innings, but their death over bowling is something they won't be too proud of. They conceded 85 runs in the last 10 overs, and India will walk to the sheds carrying the momentum with them. For the positives, though, Jayden Lennox had an outstanding international debut with figures of 1/42 in his ten overs, whereas Michael Bracewell put the breaks in that middle phase.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin. A glorious afternoon on what is a festive day in many parts of India, and out walk the two umpires. The Black Caps form a huddle before striding out to the field of play. It will be the pairing of Rohit Sharma and Shubman Gill to open the innings for India. Kyle Jamieson has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. A couple of slips in play to begin with. Let's go...

Shreyas Iyer is having a chat with the broadcasters. He says he is not trying to do anything extra and is trusting his instincts. Adds that the more time he spends practising in the nets, the better he feels when it comes to match situations. He explains that he only looks to attack when the ball is in his scoring areas and adds that there are no doubts in his mind at the moment. Reflecting on the previous game, he admits he was too focused on taking singles, which slowed his reactions, and that’s a mindset he wants to move away from going forward. Speaking about batting alongside Virat Kohli, Iyer describes their communication as always being light-hearted, but notes that they make a conscious effort to give themselves a bit of time at the crease together before shifting gears and going for shots and boundaries.

New Zealand (Playing XI) - Devon Conway, Henry Nicholls, Will Young, Daryl Mitchell, Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Hay (WK), Michael Bracewell (C), Zakary Foulkes, Kristian Clarke, Kyle Jamieson, and Jayden Lennox (ON ODI DEBUT) (In for Adithya Ashok).

India (Playing XI) - Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill (C), Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Ravindra Jadeja, KL Rahul (WK), Nitish Kumar Reddy (In for Washington Sundar), Harshit Rana, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj, and Prasidh Krishna.

Shubman Gill, the skipper of India, says that they would have batted considering their last few games here. He adds that he was feeling confident in the last game and it is always good to contribute for the team. Adds that how they came back in the middle overs in the last game was good to watch. Ends by saying that Washington Sundar misses out due to his injury and Nitish Kumar Reddy replaces him.

New Zealand captain Michael Bracewell says they have decided to bowl first, noting that the surface looks a good one to bat on. He adds that if dew sets in later in the evening, it should make batting easier under lights. Bracewell feels his side fought hard till the very end in the previous game and believes the late wickets gave them a chance of pulling things back. Looking ahead, he says the focus will be on striking in the middle overs and putting the Indian batting line-up under pressure. On playing in front of big crowds, he says it is a great challenge. He notes that the conditions are different for them, with around 40,000 fans in the stadium passionately backing the home team, but adds that the side is up for it. He also confirms one change to the XI, with Jayden Lennox coming in to make his ODI debut.
TOSS - Up goes the flip of the coin and it lands in favor of New Zealand. Michael Bracewell opts to BOWL first.

With the series on the line, the stakes couldn't be higher for both sides. Will India’s lower middle order step up again to clinch the trophy, or will the Black Caps bounce back to force a decider? Sit back and relax as we bring you all the latest updates, along with the toss and the team news from this exciting encounter in Rajkot.

New Zealand, however, will not go down without a fight. They posted a competitive total in the first game thanks to Daryl Mitchell's brilliant 84 and a strong start by their openers. Pacer Kyle Jamieson was lethal in the previous match, causing a late collapse, and the visitors will rely on him to unsettle the Indian batters again to keep the series alive.

The spotlight remains firmly on the veteran stars, with Virat Kohli fresh off a sublime 93 and Rohit Sharma looking in good touch at the top. While the batting lineup looks strong, India has been forced to make a change. All-rounder Washington Sundar is out with an injury, opening the door for the squad's new addition, Ayush Badoni. India will be happy to see Harshit Rana perform with the bat but will be hoping that the middle order is able to get them over the line in similar situations in the future.

Welcome to the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot for the second ODI between India and New Zealand! Following a nail-biting finish in Vadodara, the Men in Blue hold a 1-0 lead in this three-match series. The atmosphere is electric as the hosts look to seal the series victory right here in Rajkot.
... MATCH DAY ...

The 3-match ODI series rolls into Rajkot for the second game at the Niranjan Shah Stadium, a venue that does not see international cricket too often after replacing the Madhavrao Scindia Cricket Ground.  Only four ODIs have been played here, and the hosts have lost three. It is also a ground where chasing has been a thankless task. Targets of 300-plus have been set three times, and none have been hunted down. In fact, a team batting second is yet to win here. India's win in the first ODI was largely expected against a depleted New Zealand side, but it came with a few nerves. The hosts waited over 20 overs for their first wicket and leaked 88 runs in the final ten, areas they will want to tighten up. Also, the chase followed a similar script. When everything seemed under control with the big names doing the job, the quick loss of Virat Kohli, Ravindra Jadeja and Shreyas Iyer within 13 balls suddenly spiced things up. A handy knock from Harshit Rana and KL Rahul staying till the end ensured India crossed the line. The Black Caps can take confidence from how close they pushed India on their home turf. Batting remains New Zealand's stronger suit, and it will need to shoulder extra responsibility to shield an inexperienced bowling attack. Changes for the visitors look unlikely after just one game. India, however, are forced into one, with Washington Sundar injured and Ayush Badoni added to the squad. Nitish Kumar Reddy appears to be the likely replacement if the hosts maintain the same team composition. With history firmly favouring teams batting first, the toss could once again be crucial. Whether Rajkot sticks to the script or serves a surprise remains to be seen.
